name: Panicale (Perugia)
description: Tier 1 base, paired with Castiglione del Lago. Beautifully preserved hill town above Lago Trasimeno with strong pool-villa inventory and access to the full Trasimeno expat network.

name: La Morra (Cuneo)
description: Tier 1 Piedmont base, paired with Alba. Hill village at the heart of Barolo country with wide vineyard views and strong pool-villa inventory. Best landscape position in the Langhe.

name: Ascoli Piceno
description: Tier 2 base. Strongest expat community in Marche (300-500 full-time). Spectacular travertine city, excellent food culture. Detractor: awkward airport access and relative isolation from the broader central Italy circuit.

name: Fermo
description: Tier 2 base, paired with Ascoli Piceno. Beautiful hill town with Roman cistern and art museum. Good pool-villa inventory in surrounding hills with proximity to both the Adriatic coast and southern Sibillini.

name: Spello (Perugia)
description: Tier 3. Arguably Umbria's most beautiful small hill town. Near-zero in-town anglophone expat community. Excellent day-trip position in the Valle Umbra. Better visited from a Todi or Trasimeno base than used as a primary base.

name: Bevagna (Perugia)
description: Tier 3. Nearly untouched Roman-grid town. Pairs naturally with Spello as a day trip. No meaningful expat community or pool-villa rental market within town; countryside properties put you in the Todi catchment.

name: Cingoli (Macerata)
description: Tier 3. Known as the balcony of the Marche for panoramic views. Decent pool-villa inventory in surrounding hills. Thin, diffuse expat community. Better as a countryside stay than a named-town base.

name: Urbino
description: Tier 3. UNESCO Renaissance city and Raphael's birthplace. Thin anglophone expat community skewing academic. Montefeltro hills less cinematic than Macerata or Ascoli interior. Better as a day trip from an Ascoli/Fermo base.

name: Bagnoregio (Viterbo)
description: Tier 3. Gateway to Civita di Bagnoregio, one of Italy's most photographed villages. Day-trip only for Civita itself (11 permanent residents). Modest rental inventory in Bagnoregio proper.

name: Tuscania (Viterbo)
description: Tier 3. Heart of Etruscan civilization with necropolises and tufa-carved roads. Good pool-villa inventory in surrounding countryside. Too far from Umbria to use as an Umbrian base; best as a day trip from Bolsena or Rome.

name: Tarquinia (Viterbo)
description: Tier 3, paired with Tuscania. UNESCO Etruscan painted tombs. Best visited as a day trip from a Bolsena or Manciano base rather than used as a primary stay.

name: Sperlonga (Latina)
description: Tier 3. Stunning whitewashed coastal village above turquoise sea. Anglophone expat community essentially absent. Heavily crowded July-August. Correct for a one-week beach stay; wrong for extended base or building any social network.

name: Nizza Monferrato (Asti)
description: Tier 3. Monferrato wine country at lower prices than the Langhe. Thinner expat community and slightly less dramatic landscape than La Morra/Alba. Worth a day trip from the Langhe base; not a standalone primary destination.

name: Canelli (Asti)
description: Tier 3, paired with Nizza Monferrato. Moscato and Barbera wine country in the UNESCO Monferrato zone. Emerging pool-villa inventory. Genuinely off the tourist track. Better as a day trip from Alba than a primary base.

name: Saluzzo (Cuneo)
description: Tier 3. Beautiful and almost entirely unknown Renaissance hill town facing Monviso. Anglophone expat community near zero. Underdeveloped rental market. Best for Alpine hiking or cycling; not the right base for food-and-wine tourism.
